title: A cohesive keyboard workbench
question: Choose the workspace direction. Both preserve existing editing and generation capabilities.

options.label: Bench instrument
options.lineage: Electronics test instruments and measurement workstations
options.thesis: One stable editing frame for boards and parts, with precise controls beside the work.
options.viewport: A compact project header and stage strip frame the canvas; a quiet inspector aligns fields and keeps save visible.
options.risk: The hierarchy must stay clear when an inspector contains many technical fields.

raised.raise: Catalogue rows get a strict name, origin, and selection hierarchy.
Numeric edits remain legible and reversible throughout updates.
Every control has a clear boundary, state, and task ownership.
Stage navigation remains a small, consistent set without nested toolbars.
Dimensions and field labels align; status changes never shift the control layout.
Overlay transitions preserve canvas context and honor reduced motion.

options.label: CAD drafting console
options.thesis: Persistent object and property panes make every editing task immediately familiar.
options.viewport: An object tree, centered drawing, and fixed right inspector share one compact toolbar.
options.risk: Familiar and effective, but close to conventional CAD interfaces and less spacious.

options.label: Parts archive
options.thesis: Parts browse as labelled boxes that open into editors.
options.viewport: Labelled parts stack alongside one open part.
options.risk: Box theatrics distract from continuous geometry editing.
options.case: Keyboard designers identify less with retail shelving; repeated opening obscures placement work.
options.kept: Catalogue rows get a strict name, origin, and selection hierarchy.

options.label: Parametric notation
options.thesis: Parameters reorganize a live drawing through a field of editable notation.
options.viewport: Parameters surround a live generated keyboard.
options.risk: Typographic motion makes precision editing harder to scan.
options.case: Language-first navigation is less familiar and less clear for direct geometry manipulation.
options.kept: Numeric edits remain legible and reversible throughout updates.

options.label: Assembly notebook
options.thesis: Parts and boards live in a notebook with physical tabs.
options.viewport: A board page sits beside its component specifications.
options.risk: Decorative materials consume space needed by the drawing.
options.case: Physical page handling weakens both CAD familiarity and immediate task access.
options.kept: Every control has a clear boundary, state, and task ownership.

options.label: Four-stage sleeve
options.thesis: Four editing stages occupy a single strongly colored frame.
options.viewport: Four stage labels border a large board preview.
options.risk: Saturated surfaces compete with semantic geometry colors.
options.case: Record sleeve identity lacks keyboard-tool resonance and gives properties too little structure.
options.kept: Stage navigation remains a small, consistent set without nested toolbars.

options.label: Live parts board
options.thesis: Fixed columns align components, dimensions, and checks.
options.viewport: A component table controls a linked drawing view.
options.risk: The table becomes dominant over spatial placement.
options.case: Schedule-like browsing is less familiar for board design and delays direct manipulation.
options.kept: Dimensions and field labels align; status changes never shift the control layout.

options.label: Layer register
options.thesis: Board and part layers slide over a common drawing field.
options.viewport: A layered drawing remains under sliding property sheets.
options.risk: Overlaps can hide geometry and make small screens harder to operate.
options.case: Darkroom notation has weaker audience identification and requires translating unfamiliar states.
options.kept: Overlay transitions preserve canvas context and honor reduced motion.

canonCard.label: Standard CAD layout
canonCard.thesis: Conventional desktop CAD, with menu, toolbars, object tree and properties.
canonCard.risk: Keeps conventional density and much of the current structural language.
